    Jury walkthrough and XRPL proofs

    90-second walkthrough

    1. Initialize Testnet before the presentation. Show both mint transactions and the offers for both routes.
    2. Simulate the outage, test the 85 + 15 XRP split, then trigger the backup. Review the selected offers and verify the 80 + 20 XRP split.
    3. Co-sign and open the batch. Show both inner transactions, the backup agent’s identity, and the decision memo.
    4. Restore the normal route and retry. Verify that the retry pays 0 additional XRP, excluding fees.

    If the network slows down, open a recorded batch below and show both transactions in the explorer.

    Validated mobile batch · backup split of 80 + 20 XRP

    Both routes use the same NFTs

    Each route has its own offers for the same two NFTs. Once the NFTs transfer, their original sellers no longer own them, so the old offers cannot settle them again.

    Comparison with a centralized payment system

    A centralized system can record a single paid status per invoice and use idempotency keys with its provider. In ProofPay, competing offers refer to the same ledger assets. The atomic batch groups the NFT transfers and both payments. Participants can verify the outcome and ownership changes on the shared ledger. Both systems require prior agreement on payment terms.

    Testnet validation trials

    Primary process shutdown

    Three processes on one host hold three separate keys. The test stopped the primary process, then the backup and co-signer signed the Testnet batch. The freelancer received 80 XRP and the agency received 20 XRP. Final verification took 6.8 seconds after shutdown.

    Verify settlement after shutdown Mint PP-100 · 100 XRP Mint PP-080 · 80 XRP Outage test proof (JSON)
    Concurrent settlement submissions

    Both batches used the same client account sequence. The normal route settled and the backup received tefPAST_SEQ. After retrying the backup with a fresh sequence and the original offers, no additional XRP was paid, excluding fees.

    Verify the winning batch Verify the retry with no payout Concurrency test proof (JSON)

    AI model and deterministic rules

    In 4,096 synthetic scenarios, the exact rules accepted 2 cases. The model alone proposed 62, including 60 that violated the agreement. The rules blocked all 60. The test covers amount deviations from a few drops to 1 XRP and found no compliance gain from the model. The model ranks offers and can abstain. The exact rules control settlement.

    These transactions come from earlier trials. In Testnet mode, each new co-signed decision produces a batch with its own memo and signatures.

    Impact of the backup route

    A documented outage

    On September 30, 2026, Adyen reported payout delays affecting some clients in Brazil. The incident ended on October 2. ProofPay tests a case where another payer already has authorization to take over.

    Session measurements

    Measurements appear after a Testnet settlement.

    Proposed business pilot

    1. When a payout is blocked, how long does it usually take to pay the contractor?
    2. Who could authorize a second payer in advance, and for which invoices?
    3. What proof would you need to verify the settlement and reconcile the invoice?

    Use a real, anonymized incident. Record when the payout was blocked and restored, how long settlement took, and who had authority to pay. Replay the incident with test data and measure time to confirmation from the same start point. Record the payout per recipient, retries, and fees. Track the time spent on human approval separately from XRPL confirmation.

    Pilot success criteria. Both recipients receive the agreed amounts, a retry produces no additional payout, the co-signer is identifiable, and both invoices reconcile. Compare recovery time with the original incident and ask the business owner to approve the backup scenario explicitly.
